html:
Northern Rhodesia was the British territory north of the Zambezi that became Zambia, run by the British South Africa Company until 1924 and then as a protectorate under the Colonial Office.

The company's two territories were joined in 1911. At first the land served mainly as a source of migrant labour for the mines and farms of Southern Rhodesia and South Africa. From the late 1920s the Copperbelt mines changed that, and white settlers and miners came in numbers.

In 1953 it was put into the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, against African wishes. Protest led by Kenneth Kaunda broke the federation, and the territory became independent as Zambia on 24 October 1964.
sum: Northern Rhodesia was the British territory north of the Zambezi that became Zambia, run by the British South Africa Company until 1924 and then as a protectorate under the Colonial Office.
